questions.question:
What will be the value of the given expression if ‘A’ means ‘+’, ‘B’ means ‘–’, ‘C’ means ‘×’, and ‘D’ means ‘÷’?

44 A 7 B (9 C 7) A (24 B 19) A (18 D 6) C 4
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

 
 

 **Alphabet**
 A
 B
 C
 D
 
 

 **Operators**
 +
 -
 × 
 ÷ 
 
 

Given expression : 44 A 7 B (9 C 7) A (24 B 19) A (18 D 6) C 4

After replacing the mathematical operators in place of alphabets in given expression is as follows : 44 + 7 - (9 × 7) + (24 - 19) + (18 ÷ 6) × 4

= 44 + 7 - __**(9 × 7)**__ + __**(24 - 19)**__ + __**(18 ÷ 6)**__ × 4

= 44 + 7 - 63 + 5 + __**3 × 4**__

= __**44 + 7**__ - 63 __**+ 5 + 12**__

= __**68 - 63**__

**= 5**

Hence, the correct answer is **"5".**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

I __have completed__ the work two hours ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**completed**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **tense** in the sentence "I **have completed** the work two hours ago" is **present perfect tense.**
 
• **The present perfect tense** is used if the action **started in the past** but still has an **effect on the present**.
 
 
• **Example:** *I** have wanted** to go to the market since yesterday.*
 
 
 
• There is **no action** going on in the **present** according to the** given sentence** as the **work** has already been **completed** two hours ago. 
 
• This demands the usage of **simple past tense**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Mark **slept** like a baby yesterday. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, "completed" is the appropriate option as it is in the simple past tense. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past tense** is divided into four types; **simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.**
 
• **Simple Past tense** - denotes the completed action.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **ate **ice cream.*
 
 
 
• **Past Continuous tense** - denotes that the action was going on for some time but is over now.
 
 
• **Example:** *I **was eating** ice cream.*
 
 
 
• **Past Perfect tense** - denotes the action that has been completed sometime before the past.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **had eaten** ice cream before knowing it was unhealthy. *
 
 
 
• **Past Perfect Continuous tense **- denotes that the past action had continued sometime in the past.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **had been eating** ice cream before I caught cold. *
